answer: Trust that must travel along real links can't be inflated by adding names, since fakes touch the honest network only where real agents accepted them. Here a quartz-grading job is offered by a random walk: each agent hands the request to one contact, and the thread of handoffs stops where it lands. Three thousand fakes linked densely to one another hang off the honest web like a vine off two nails, and almost no request ever climbs in.
